column1: # queue_job_v5_COLUMNS.tsv: every output column of queue_job_v5 (Agentic/tree/ALARM_DESIGN/KIT_V5/tools/queue_job_v5.py). Generated by _tools/agent_docs_v1.py: file, column and source_line come from the code; meaning, unit, known_at and empty_means are written by hand from the code (a quote in backticks is a quote of the code) and kept when the generator runs again. TEST, NOT REVIEWED.
# archive/ holds past editions: read only, never run; to rerun one, use the old release install.

column3: meaning
column5: known_at

column3: the row's stamp: `the utc stamp taken from the clock inside this call` (reg_append_v1.py)
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN
column6: never empty: `THE STAMP COMES FROM THE CLOCK: do not give`

column3: the job twin under the run folder (`'job': os.path.relpath(twin, run)`), named `'%s_judge_%s_%s_%s.job.sh' % (n, seat, kind, idea)`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: the twin's sha16: `'job_sha16': js` with `js = sha16(twin)`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: the job's kind: `only the kinds that have a V6 template are queued (COUNT and CLEAN)`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: the idea of a COUNT job; for CLEAN `IDEA is a label`
column4: name: `capitals and digits only, starting with a letter`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: COUNT: the variants counted; CLEAN: the jobs it cleans (`'variants': ','.join(vs)`)
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: the queue it went into: `a Q_V queue (default: the first empty one of Q_V1..Q_V21)`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: the PREREG file of the job's variants, for the kinds that are not clean yet (`ONE PREREG A JOB`)
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: that PREREG file's sha16 as VARIANTS sealed it (`'@@PREREG_SHA@@': psha`)
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: what the job declares it writes (its `# WRITES_MB: @@WMB@@` line): COUNT `'@@WMB@@': str(300 * n)`, CLEAN `'@@WMB@@': '10'`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: the memory the job declares (`# MEM_MB: @@MMB@@`): COUNT `'@@MMB@@': '6000'`, CLEAN `'@@MMB@@': '1000'`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: the minutes the job declares (`declared minutes: @@MINUTES@@`): COUNT `'@@MINUTES@@': str(10 * n)`, CLEAN `'@@MINUTES@@': '5'`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: the job template's sha16, checked against the code's pin (`tsha != TEMPLATE_SHA[kind]`): `a KIND without one is NOT CLEAN YET`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: the job this one reads, for the kinds that are not clean yet: `'from_job': opts['--from-job'] or '-'`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN

column3: where the job writes its receipts: `'receipts_rel': 'receipts/%s_%s_%s' % (n, kind, idea)`
column5: at queue time, when the row is appended: the tool `writes the twin to RUN/jobs/, the RUNS row through reg_append_v1.py` before it copies the job into IN
column6: never empty (the folder fills when the job runs)

column3: the stage (`STAGES.tsv (every stage with rc)`): COUNT `st start 0 0`, `st detect_${V}_$hv`, `st count_$V`, `st end 0 0`; CLEAN: no job since ALARM_V1_8 (its template is in archive/); a pinned file that changed `st pin 3 0`
column5: as the job runs, one line per stage; the file is whole at its end line (`done when receipts/%s_%s_%s/STAGES.tsv has its end line`)

column3: the stage's exit code: 0 ok; `st pin 3 0` a pinned file changed; `st count_$V 5 0` detection failed; `st disk_$V 7 0` SCRATCH too full
column5: as the job runs, one line per stage; the file is whole at its end line (`done when receipts/%s_%s_%s/STAGES.tsv has its end line`)

column3: the stage's run time: `$(( $(date +%s)-t0 ))`; 0 for a stage that is not timed
column5: as the job runs, one line per stage; the file is whole at its end line (`done when receipts/%s_%s_%s/STAGES.tsv has its end line`)

column3: the clock when the line is written: `$(date -u +%FT%TZ)`
column5: as the job runs, one line per stage; the file is whole at its end line (`done when receipts/%s_%s_%s/STAGES.tsv has its end line`)

column3: free text: the start's `SCRATCH_DISK free ${f} MB`, a detection's last log line, a count's ALL row, the end's free space
column5: as the job runs, one line per stage; the file is whole at its end line (`done when receipts/%s_%s_%s/STAGES.tsv has its end line`)

column3: the month of the fires, from their t: `split("2509 2510 2511 2512",m," ")` with month starts `split("1757462400 1759276800 1761955200 1764547200 1767225600",b," ")`; then one `ALL` row
column5: when the job's count stage of that variant ends (`st count_$V`)

column3: fires in the month: `fires, waves and coins per month on 10 Sep-31 Dec 2025`, `by detection only`
column5: when the job's count stage of that variant ends (`st count_$V`)

column3: `waves: a fire more than 1800 s after the previous fire (any coin) starts a new wave (labcore.waves); a wave counts in the month of its first fire`
column5: when the job's count stage of that variant ends (`st count_$V`)

column3: coins with a fire in the month (`nc[k]++` once per month and coin); in the ALL row, coins over the four months (`nca`)
column5: when the job's count stage of that variant ends (`st count_$V`)

column3: the most fires in one wave: `if (cur>mx[wk]) mx[wk]=cur`
column5: when the job's count stage of that variant ends (`st count_$V`)

column3: fires on BTC: `if ($1=="BTC") nb[k]++`
column5: when the job's count stage of that variant ends (`st count_$V`)

column3: NOT DOCUMENTED IN CODE: the first column of detect.py's fire list; the job checks the header `if ($1!="coin" || $2!="t")`
column5: when the job's count stage of that variant ends (`head -n 21 $W/${V}_FIRES_COUNT.tsv`)

column3: NOT DOCUMENTED IN CODE: the second column of detect.py's fire list; the job sorts by it (`sort -t$'\t' -k2,2n -k1,1`) and compares it with the month starts
column4: epoch seconds: compared with `1757462400` (10 Sep 2025 00:00 UTC)
column5: when the job's count stage of that variant ends (`head -n 21 $W/${V}_FIRES_COUNT.tsv`)

column3: the MB the job's scratch folder holds at its end (`du -sm $W`); the queue reads it: `MB of this run's own uncleaned scratch: measured (receipts DISK.tsv and STORE_PLACES.tsv) for finished jobs, declared for others`
column5: at the job's end, just before its end line (`du -sm $W`)

column3: SCRATCH free at the end: `fmb(){ df -m @@SCRATCH@@ | awk 'NR==2{print $4}'; }`
column5: at the job's end, just before its end line (`du -sm $W`)
